title: Towards a Benchmark for Fire Safety Code Interpretation in the Hong Kong AEC Industry
abstract: arXiv:2610.16127v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly explored in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) domain, yet their reliability in regulatory compliance remains uncertain. In this study, we evaluate the performance of LLMs on Hong Kong fire safety codes. In collaboration with domain experts, we create a localized benchmark dataset comprising both multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and open-ended questions (OEQs) to evaluate 12 widely used proprietary and open-source models. Our findings show that top-performing proprietary models achieve 80-90% accuracy on MCQs, whereas open-source models generally lag behind. However, on open-ended evaluation, expert human assessments reveal an accuracy range of only 50-70%, demonstrating that LLMs still have substantial room for improvement in specialized compliance tasks.

translated_title: 迈向香港建筑、工程及建造业消防安全规范解读的基准测试
translated_abstract: 大语言模型在建筑、工程和建造领域的应用探索日益增多，但其在法规合规方面的可靠性仍不确定。在本研究中，我们评估了大语言模型在香港消防安全规范方面的表现。我们与领域专家合作，创建了一个包含多项选择题和开放式问题的本地化基准数据集，用于评估12个广泛使用的专有和开源模型。我们的研究结果表明，表现最佳的专有模型在多项选择题上达到80-90%的准确率，而开源模型普遍落后。然而，在开放式评估中，专家人工评估显示准确率仅为50-70%，这表明大语言模型在专业合规任务方面仍有很大的改进空间。
tldr: 本研究创建了香港消防安全规范的本地化基准数据集并评估12个大语言模型，发现专有模型在多项选择题上可达80-90%准确率，但开放式问题的专家评估准确率仅为50-70%，表明大语言模型在专业法规合规任务上仍有显著提升空间。
en_tdlr: This study creates a localized benchmark dataset for Hong Kong fire safety codes to evaluate 12 LLMs, revealing that top proprietary models achieve 80-90% accuracy on MCQs but only 50-70% accuracy on open-ended questions per expert assessment, demonstrating substantial room for improvement in specialized compliance tasks.
